findings.evidence: Also, you submit the request in the portal. Countersign the employee request within two business days. You track its status there until the payment clears.
findings.fix: Split the paragraph so the employee's steps (submit, track) and the manager's step (countersign) sit in clearly separated parts, or name the manager as the subject of the countersign sentence.
findings.violation: The paragraph addresses the employee reader directly as you, then inserts an imperative, countersign the employee request, that only the approving manager can carry out (per Approval Timeline, the manager is the one who signs), with no signal marking the shift, so a reader cannot tell which sentence is theirs to act on.

findings.evidence: The benefits team coordinates every stipend request from intake to payout.
findings.fix: Rewrite the opening sentence to state the topic the rest of the paragraph covers.
findings.violation: The paragraph's opening sentence shares almost no vocabulary with the rest of the paragraph, so it does not preview the paragraph's actual topic.

findings.evidence: A separate audit last spring reviewed unrelated travel expenses. Federal guidance on remote work continues to evolve each year. The office coffee budget was reset at the start of the quarter.
findings.fix: Remove the three unrelated sentences, or move each to a section its own topic belongs to.
findings.violation: After its opening sentence on stipend-request coordination, the section moves through a travel-expense audit, federal remote-work guidance, and the office coffee budget, three unrelated themes with no signal connecting any of them back to stipend coordination, so a reader finishing the section cannot state what it was actually about.

findings.evidence: The benefits team coordinates every stipend request from intake to payout. A separate audit last spring reviewed unrelated travel expenses. Federal guidance on remote work continues to evolve each year. The office coffee budget was reset at the start of the quarter.
findings.fix: Rewrite the paragraph so each sentence's subject connects to the topic the prior sentence just introduced, or delete the sentences that do not belong to the paragraph's own topic.
findings.violation: Each of the four sentences opens with a new subject, the benefits team, a separate audit, federal guidance, the office coffee budget, with no sentence picking up the topic the one before it just established, so the reader has to re-orient at every sentence boundary.

findings.evidence: The finance liaison publishes the vendor list on the first business day of the month. The most recent version supersedes the one that came before it.
findings.fix: State explicitly whether the vendor list and the equipment catalog are the same document, or describe each distinctly enough that a reader can tell them apart without cross-checking.
findings.violation: This sentence describes the vendor list with the identical publishing cadence and supersession wording the Program Overview section uses for the equipment catalog, with no signal for whether vendor list and equipment catalog name the same resource or two different ones.

findings.evidence: You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the reimbursable item against the request log each month. Payroll releases the covered purchase amount after that monthly review.
findings.fix: Use one term for the object across all three sentences, or state explicitly that the three names refer to the same item.
findings.violation: Three different terms, stipend item, reimbursable item, and covered purchase amount, name what reads as the same object across three consecutive process steps, with no defined-terms signal that the three names mean the same thing, so a reader has to check rather than being told.
